title: GPU surge playbook and fleet health log - Week of 2026-03-09
content:
Purpose:
Weekly combined notes: surge readiness checklist, short-term capacity moves, recent node health anomalies, and playbook tweaks for regional failover (US-W, EU-C, AP-S). This lives as the canonical ops checklist for the next two sprints while we complete the capacity projection change.

Attendees:
- Aisha Patel (owner)
- Rafael Gomez (oncall infra)
- Lina Chen (SRE)
- Marcus Lee (capacity planning)
- Julie Park (release eng, notes)

High-level status (as of 2026-03-12):
- Overall fleet healthy but signs of elevated node churn in eu-central after recent kernel roll (kernel-6.2.14).
- Effective GPU capacity: ~420 H100 SXM (120 nodes), 260 A100 80G (65 nodes). Estimated available capacity for hosted tenants after reservations: 640 GPUs (approx).
- Short-term surge capacity: can free ~60 GPUs within 48 hours by reprovisioning low-priority dedicated pools and applying aggressive preemption policy.

Recent incidents / anomalies:
1) 2026-03-11: eu-central kernel upgrade triggered 7 nodes to repeatedly OOM on startup (symptom: nv_peer_mem init fail). Ticket: JIRA-INFRA-783. Impact: transient <1% capacity loss for 2 hours; some small-hosted jobs retried 3x. RCA: kernel+nv driver mismatch in tenant-image base. Action: rollback kernel on affected nodes and pin driver version in node bootstrap.
2) 2026-03-09: increased tail latency for short-chat workloads in us-west during backup window. Root cause: backup snapshot I/O contended with NVMe-local caching on 5 nodes. Mitigation: moved snapshot windows and limited caching flush to off-peak.

Capacity planning notes and decisions:
- Marcus: projection updated with 20% Q2 demand growth for generative-chat workloads. We will schedule a small capacity add in eu-central (10 H100 nodes) to avoid sustained hotspots.
- Prioritization: postpone non-critical expansion in AP-S until after quantization job (PR: github.com/redwood/ops/PR-412).
- Reserve policy change approved (draft): reduce dedicated reserve buffers from 15% to 10% for 3-week trial to improve available capacity for hosted bursts. (Follow-up: INFRA-790 to instrument risks).

Surge playbook (quick steps for <72h surge):
1) Trigger: on-call flags sustained 90p token consumption > 75% for 6 hours.
2) Run quick reclaim script: infra/reclaim-lowprio.sh (evict & reprovision non-critical dedicated pools). Owner: Rafael. Expected free: ~40-60 GPUs.
3) Apply dynamic preemption policy through the scheduler: preempt-level=medium. Owner: Lina.
4) Route excess short-tail requests to compatible smaller-parameter model (redwood-compat/llama-13b-q4) for latency-sensitive routes. Requires model routing rule: ROUTE-225.
5) Notify customers via status page and targeted email for affected Dedicated tenants. Owner: Julie.
6) Post-surge: run health sweep and run NVMe scrub on nodes that entered heavy I/O. Owner: SRE team.

Node health & maintenance log (this week):
- Rebooted 5 eu-central nodes (node-ec-042..046) due to nv_peer_mem errors; kernels rolled back.
- Reimaged 2 us-west nodes to resolve GPU thermal throttling caused by bad fan-profile; replaced fans scheduled next week (ticket: HW-RMA-1211).
- Replaced failing BMC on node-ap-011; completed hardware verification.

Action items (owners and due dates):
- Aisha: finalize reserve-buffer trial parameters and publish runbook (due 2026-03-15). (JIRA-INFRA-790).
- Rafael: complete reclaim script dry-run and post logs to /confluence/gpu-reclaims (due 2026-03-13).
- Lina: add kernel-driver compatibility checks to node bootstrap pipeline and add alert for nv_peer_mem failures (due 2026-03-17).
- Marcus: finalize Q2 capacity purchase order for eu-central and confirm procurement timelines (due 2026-03-20).
- Julie: update status page template to include estimated time-to-capacity when surge mitigation is invoked (due 2026-03-14).

Open questions / risks:
- If reserve buffer trial increases eviction churn, we need a safety rollback trigger (metric: eviction-rate > 4% of nodes within 24h).
- AP-S region quantization jobs could create sustained CPU pressure that blocks node reprovisioning. Proposed mitigation: dedicated CPU-limited node pool for ETL/quant jobs.

Knowledge & followups:
- Link to surge simulation results: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/Surge+Sim+Mar2026
- Add a short postmortem for the eu-central kernel roll to the incident timeline (owner: Rafael).
- Cross-team sync: schedule meeting with release-engineering to coordinate kernel rollouts (action owner: Aisha).

Next meeting:
- Weekly capacity sync: 2026-03-16 10:00 PT (agenda: review reserve-trial telemetry, eu-central node add, AP-S quantization gating).

Notes to self (raw):
- Watch eviction latency during reserve trial; keep an eye on the 95p preemption time.
- Consider automated canary of kernel on a single maintenance node before wide rollout.

End of log.
